answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake and build a verifiable work record before it can trade at scale. Like a grove that grows slowly, reputation accrues only through completed, attested jobs, so a newcomer cannot instantly appear trustworthy. A periodic beacon check publishes each agent's stake and history, making duplicates visible, while a sudden comet-like burst of new identities triggers rate limits and extra verification. Creating thousands of fakes then costs real locked capital and time, far more than any single fraud gains.
